input.story: I deliver food for an app in Jaipur. They deactivated my ID last week and are holding 8,500 of my earnings for the last 2 weeks. Support just sends automated replies. Am I an employee? Can I claim salary?

output.masked_story: I deliver food for an app in Jaipur. They deactivated my ID last week and are holding 8,500 of my earnings for the last 2 weeks. Support just sends automated replies. Am I an employee? Can I claim salary?

case.summary: The user works as a food delivery partner for an app in Jaipur. Their account was deactivated last week and the platform is withholding INR 8500 earned over the past two weeks. Support responses are only automated.
case.user_goal: To get the withheld earnings released and understand if they can claim them as salary.

timeline.event: User contacted support and received automated replies

evidence_missing: Payment statement showing the INR 8500 earned
follow_up_questions: When exactly was your account deactivated (date)?
Did you receive any written notice or email about the deactivation?
Do you have screenshots of your earnings and the deactivation message?
What is the name of the food‑delivery app you work for?

lines: Other dues (leave encashment, reimbursements, etc.): Rs 8,500
notes: Check your offer letter/payslips for the exact gross vs in-hand salary. Gratuity, if any, has separate rules - ask a lawyer.
Interest on delayed money may be claimable; the rate is for a lawyer/court to decide, so we don't add it here.

assessment.where_you_stand: You are a gig worker who earned INR 8,500 in the last two weeks, but the platform deactivated your account and is now withholding that money. The platform’s action can be seen as a breach of the contract you have with it, so you may claim compensation for the loss under the Indian Contract Act, 1872 [KB:ica_s73]. Since the earnings are essentially wages, the Code on Wages, 2019 requires payment of wages within 2 working days after termination [KB:cow_s17]. You can file a claim for the unpaid amount within 3 years before the labour authority [KB:cow_s45]. Strengths: you have a clear amount (₹8,500) and a written contract/terms of service with the app. Weaknesses: you currently lack screenshots of the earnings and the deactivation notice, which are needed as proof.

options.title: Collect evidence
options.what_to_do: Take screenshots of the deactivation notice, your earnings statement, and any chat or email with the platform. Save them as PDFs or images.

options.title: Send a formal written demand
options.what_to_do: Draft a polite but firm email or registered letter to the platform’s support/legal team stating: you earned ₹8,500, your account was deactivated on 13‑Nov‑2026, you request payment within 7 days, and you will approach the labour authority if not resolved.
needs: email address or postal address of the platform

options.title: File a claim with the Labour Department
options.what_to_do: If the platform does not pay, submit a written complaint to the Rajasthan Labour Commissioner (or nearest labour office). Attach your evidence and the demand letter. The claim must be filed within 3 years of the breach [KB:cow_s45].
options.time: 1-2 weeks for filing, then variable for resolution
options.cost: court/authority fee (minimal) and possible travel cost

options.title: Seek free legal aid
options.what_to_do: If you need help preparing the claim, call the Legal Services Authority helpline 15100 or visit a Common Service Centre for free advice [KB:lsa_s12_legal_aid].
options.time: same day to a few days

proof_tips: Ask the app’s support via WhatsApp or email to confirm the deactivation date and reason in writing.
Take a screenshot of the ‘Earnings’ page showing the ₹8,500 pending payout.
Save any push notifications or SMS you received about the account status.
what_i_dont_know: The exact terms of your gig contract (e.g., notice period, termination clause).
Whether the platform has a specific grievance redressal mechanism mandated by its own policy.
If any state-specific labour rules in Rajasthan modify the general Code on Wages [KB:cow_s17] provisions.
assessment.needs_lawyer_reason: For the initial steps—collecting proof, sending a demand, and filing a labour‑department complaint—you can act yourself. A lawyer becomes useful if the platform contests the claim or you need to pursue court action.
assessment.reply: You earned ₹8,500 as a food‑delivery partner, but the app deactivated your account on 13 Nov 2026 and is now holding that money. This is a breach of your contract, and under the Indian Contract Act you can claim the loss [KB:ica_s73]. Because the amount is wages, the Code on Wages says it should be paid within 2 working days after termination [KB:cow_s17], and you may file a claim with the labour authority within 3 years [KB:cow_s45].
